consensus_summary: Dew primarily symbolizes divine blessing, favor, refreshment, provision, and life-giving grace; common alternatives include God’s word/teaching (Deut 32:2), transience of devotion, and minority senses such as resurrection or the Spirit.
book_summary: Dew is the word descending silently from heaven by night and found in the morning; manna falls on it and, when the dew lifts, the word remains as daily bread that evaporates without root once the sun grows hot.
consensus_core_identification: divine blessing, favor, and refreshing grace
book_core_identification: the Word of God descending from heaven
boundary_disagreement: Book elevates the word/doctrine sense (only an alternative in consensus) to the sole core, fuses it with the manna-as-word complex and a no-root evaporation motif, and sets aside blessing/refreshment as the leading identification.
material_contradiction: Consensus primary referent is divine blessing/grace; book primary referent is the descending Word. These are distinct identifications; accepting the book replaces the consensus core.
rationale: Minimum cores differ: blessing/grace versus the Word. Although consensus lists ‘word/teaching’ as a common alternative, its settled primary identification remains blessing. The book explicitly contrasts its reading with the common blessing/Spirit view and develops a distinct Word-plus-manna-plus-evaporation complex. This is replacement of the central referent, not preservation with narrowed or broadened boundaries, hence DIVERGENT.
strongest_objection: Because the word-as-dew reading is already attested as a common alternative, the book might be classified as merely elevating and elaborating an existing strand (REFINED) rather than a true core contradiction.
